scenarios.context: A newcomer visits a flat with a letting agent.

speakerA.en: Welcome. This is the flat I mentioned. It has two bedrooms, a living room and a small balcony.
The rent is nine hundred a month, and water is included. You pay for electricity, gas and the internet separately.
It's equal to one month's rent. It's returned at the end of the tenancy, provided that there's no damage.
Certainly. The minimum contract is twelve months, and you must give one month's notice if you want to leave.
It's partly furnished, with a kitchen, a wardrobe and a bed. Small pets are allowed, but you'd need written permission.
Yes, and I recommend taking photos on the day you move in, so that you aren't charged for existing damage.

speakerB.en: It looks bright and spacious. How much is the monthly rent, and are bills included?
I see. How much is the deposit, and when would I get it back?
Could I take a look at the contract before signing? I'd like to understand the notice period.
Is the flat furnished? And are pets allowed?
That's fine. Would it be possible to see the inventory of everything in the flat?
Good advice. I'd like to think it over and give you an answer by tomorrow.

scenarios.context: A newcomer opens a current account at a bank.

speakerA.en: Good afternoon. How can I help you today?
Certainly. Do you have your passport and proof of address with you?
Yes, a signed tenancy agreement is fine. Are you working or studying?
That would be helpful. Would you like a debit card and online banking as well?
There's no monthly fee for this account, but international transfers have a small charge, depending on the amount.
It should arrive by post within a week, and you'll receive the PIN separately for security reasons.

speakerB.en: I've recently moved here, and I'd like to open a current account, please.
I have my passport and my residence permit, but I don't have a utility bill yet. Would a tenancy agreement be acceptable?
I'm starting a job next month. I can bring the employment contract later if that's necessary.
Yes, both, please. Are there any monthly fees or charges for sending money abroad?
I see. How long will it take before I can use the card?
Thank you. Could you also explain how to set up a direct debit for my rent?

scenarios.context: A newcomer registers as a patient at a health centre.

speakerA.en: Good morning, health centre. How can I help you?
Of course. Have you brought some form of identification and proof of address?
That's fine. Please fill in this form with your medical history and any medication you're taking.
Yes, once the doctor has reviewed your records. I recommend booking a first appointment as soon as possible.
There's a slot next Tuesday at ten fifteen, but if it's urgent, we also have a same-day phone consultation.
You can call our out-of-hours number, and in an emergency, you should dial the emergency services immediately.

speakerB.en: Hello. I've just moved to the area, and I'd like to register as a patient.
Yes, I have my passport and a copy of my rental agreement. Is that sufficient?
I take medication for high blood pressure. Will I be able to get a repeat prescription here?
What is the earliest appointment available?
Tuesday will be fine. And what should I do if I need medical help outside opening hours?
Thank you. Do I need to bring my medical records from my previous country?

scenarios.context: A resident applies to extend a residence permit.

speakerA.en: Next, please. Good morning. What can I do for you?
May I see your appointment confirmation and your passport, please?
Thank you. Have you got the application form, and is it completed in full?
Everything seems to be in order, but I'll need your fingerprints. Please place your fingers on the scanner.
Usually between four and eight weeks. You'll receive a letter when your permit is ready for collection.
Yes, as long as your current permit was valid when you applied. Keep this receipt, and call the helpline on the leaflet if you have any problems.

speakerB.en: Good morning. I have an appointment to apply for an extension of my residence permit.
Here you are. I've also brought my employment contract, my recent payslips and proof of my address.
Yes, I filled it in online and printed it. I also have two passport-sized photographs.
Of course. How long does the process normally take?
Am I allowed to continue working while my application is being processed?
Thank you. I'll keep it somewhere safe and call the helpline if I have any questions.

scenarios.context: A newcomer chooses a mobile phone plan in a shop.

speakerA.en: Good morning. I'd like to get a mobile phone plan, preferably one that doesn't require a long contract.
What's the difference? I don't know how the system works here.
And with a prepaid plan?
I think the prepaid plan suits me better, since I'm not sure how long I'll stay in this city.
I use quite a lot of data, and I call my family overseas every week.
That sounds suitable. Do I need to show any identification to activate the SIM card?

speakerB.en: We have several options. Do you want a monthly contract or a prepaid plan?
With a contract, you pay a fixed fee every month for twenty-four months, and you often get a new phone included.
You top up your credit whenever you want, and you can cancel at any time, but the phone isn't included.
Understood. How much data do you usually use? Do you make a lot of calls abroad?
Then I'd recommend this plan. It includes unlimited data and cheap international calls to many countries.
Yes, your passport and proof of address, please. It will only take a few minutes.
